verse.verse_3: and the even and the odd,
verse.verse_4: and by the night when it departs.
verse.verse_5: Is there in this an oath for one endowed with understanding?
verse.verse_6: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with Ad
verse.verse_7: of Iram, known for their lofty columns,
verse.verse_8: the like of whom no nation was ever created in the lands of the world?
verse.verse_9: And how did He deal with Thamud who hewed out rocks in the valley?
verse.verse_10: And with Pharaoh of the tent pegs
verse.verse_11: who transgressed in the countries of the world
verse.verse_13: Then their Lord unloosed upon them the lash of chastisement.
verse.verse_14: Truly your Lord is ever watchful.
verse.verse_15: As for man, when his Lord tests him by exalting him and bestowing His bounties upon him, he says: “My Lord has exalted me.”
verse.verse_16: But when He tests him by straitening his sustenance, he says: “My Lord has humiliated me.”
verse.verse_17: But no; you do not treat the orphan honourably,
verse.verse_18: and do not urge one another to feed the poor,
verse.verse_19: and greedily devour the entire inheritance,
verse.verse_20: and love the riches, loving them ardently.
verse.verse_21: But no; when the earth is ground to powder,
verse.verse_22: and when your Lord appears with rows upon rows of angels,
verse.verse_23: and when Hell is brought near that Day. On that Day will man understand, but of what avail will that understanding be?
verse.verse_24: He will say: “Would that I had sent ahead what would be of avail for this life of mine!”
verse.verse_25: Then on that Day Allah will chastise as none other can chastise;
verse.verse_26: and Allah will bind as none other can bind.
verse.verse_27: (On the other hand it will be said): “O serene soul!
verse.verse_28: Return to your Lord well-pleased (with your blissful destination), well-pleasing (to your Lord).
